formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once anyone submits the signature to permit(), the owner's axl-wstETH allowance for the spender is set to exactly `value`, replacing any earlier allowance (ERC20Permit.permit -> _approve(issuer, spender, value)).
The spender can then move up to `value` axl-wstETH from the owner with transferFrom. A value of type(uint256).max is never used up; any other value goes down with each transfer (ERC20.transferFrom).
The signature only works until `deadline` (block.timestamp > deadline reverts), and only once, because nonces[owner] goes up by one when it is used.
formats.shown: "Authorize spending of tokens", then the spender address, the max amount in axl-wstETH ("Unlimited" from 2^255 up), the deadline as a date, and the owner. The nonce is hidden.

findings.title: Permit: metadata.owner names Lido's wstETH, but the contract is Axelar's bridged wrapper token.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json metadata.owner "Wrapped liquid staked Ether 2.0". meta.json gives fullyQualifiedName BurnableMintableCappedERC20 with constructor name "Axelar Wrapped wstETH" and symbol "axl-wstETH", and the descriptor's own domain.name is "Axelar Wrapped wstETH". Case 0's screen shows the owner as "Wrapped liquid staked Ether 2.0" next to an amount in axl-wstETH.

findings.title: Permit: no interpolatedIntent, so the glance line names neither the spender nor the amount.
findings.evidence: descriptor.json format Permit: "intent": "Authorize spending of tokens", and there is no interpolatedIntent. The amount and spender appear only in the fields.
